text:
marcus: quick q — when a request falls back from hosted -> private, who is responsible for applying policy labels (quota, tier, customer_id)?

sophia: good catch. i think control-plane should attach labels before routing so telemetry doesn't lose provenance. avoids per-runtime replication. :thinking_face:

priya: that works unless the private runtime enforces stricter policy and needs to augment labels (e.g., local contract). how do we avoid double-counting?

ben: option A: control-plane labels + hop header X-Policy-Source=controlplane. Option B: let runtime own final labels and return a delta in response headers for billing. A feels simpler for routing.

marcus: leaning A. simpler and keeps routing decisions local to control-plane. but we must ensure private runtimes can reject and return clear error codes that control-plane translates.

priya: agree on rejects. also we need a canonical audit field preserved end-to-end: X-Customer-ID and X-Request-UUID. otherwise downstream logging fragments.

ben: implementation sketch: control-plane injects:

```
X-Customer-ID: cust_123
X-Request-UUID: 7f4a2b
X-Policy-Source: controlplane
X-Policy-Signature: sig_v1(base64)
```

sophia: the signature is important for tamper detection in private/on-prem. but how do we handle key distribution for sig_v1 to private? KMS/HSM per-tenant or rotate ephemeral certs?

marcus: proposal: short-lived mTLS certs (48h) issued by our control-plane CA + an optional HSM binding for enterprise. control-plane rotates and pushes certs during provisioning.

priya: +1. fallback: if cert push fails, runtime can fall back to a transient allowlist but mark telemetry as 'unverified' so we can alert.

ben: edge-case: Dedicated pools might want internal-only identities (no external customer id). Should we allow an identity translation table in the manifest?

marcus: yes, manifest-level translation allowed but must be opt-in and audited. manifest example: 

```
manifest:
  identity_translation:
    - from: external_customer_id
      to: internal_account
      audit: true
```

sophia: another concern — rate limiter placement. If we pre-label at control-plane but enforce at private runtime, we need atomic counters to avoid races. Suggestions?

priya: use a token-bucket lease API: control-plane mints a short-lived "rate token" with capacity and expiry; runtime consumes tokens and reports back usage. simplest across network.

ben: that'll add latency but only for bursty routes. we can make token checks optional per-route. document recommended defaults.

marcus: ops items:
- define X-Policy-* header spec + signature format
- cert lifecycle doc for private/dedicated
- implement token-bucket lease prototype in control-plane
- fallback telemetry flag for unverified hops

sophia: I'll draft the RFC follow-up with the header spec and failure semantics. expect a rough PR by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: FYI: deploy-canary scheduled for dedicated/region-3 at 2025-06-02 18:00:00 UTC — will exercise header injection path.

ben: great — can we add a smoke test that intentionally corrupts X-Policy-Signature to validate unverified telemetry?

priya: yes, add an integration test in infra/e2e that toggles cert push and asserts telemetry flags.

marcus: thanks all. will sync with infra tomorrow to scope the prototype.
